capabilities: Convert a Markdown table into one note per row via context menu or command palette
Map columns to frontmatter properties with declared types (text, number, date, checkbox, tags)
Create and reuse a .base file that collects the generated notes under a shared tag
Control output folder, name column, and base tag, with {{date:FORMAT}} templates
Avoid overwriting by suffixing duplicate note names
disambiguation: Not a table editor; it only reads an existing Markdown table and generates notes and a .base file from it.
extras: README includes manual installation steps (npm build, copying files) and notes the interface supports English and Portuguese.
intentEvidence: Turn a Markdown table into organized notes and track them in a Base.
problem: Creating a set of related notes by hand is repetitive, and Obsidian offers no way to turn a planning table into notes plus a Base view in one step.

relations.evidence: Turn a Markdown table into organized notes and track them in a Base.

summary: Table-to-notes converter that turns a Markdown table into one note per row with frontmatter properties and an Obsidian Base that tracks them.
